findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from request context and get cancelled
findings.body: All four goroutines (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) build their timeout context from the incoming request `ctx`. The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which typically happens before the goroutine completes its legacy write. The legacy store write will therefore frequently be aborted mid-flight, silently losing the data that mode 3 is supposed to keep in sync. Use a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a fresh background context carrying the needed request values) before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Storage failure recorded as legacy duration in Create/Update
findings.body: In Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) the error path for the *storage* call calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. This attributes unified-storage failures/latency to the legacy backend metric, making the dashboards and error rates for both backends wrong. Should be `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

findings.title: Delete passes object name as the 'kind' metric label
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the resource `name` where every other call site passes `options.Kind`. This both mislabels the metric and causes unbounded label cardinality (one time-series per object name), which can blow up the Prometheus registry.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records storage duration
findings.body: Inside the async legacy DeleteCollection the code calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` with `startLegacy`. This records legacy latency/errors under the storage metric, double-counting storage and hiding legacy failures. Should be `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Delete puts the un-enriched logger into the context
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses `d.Log` instead of the `log` built on line 96, so downstream code reading the logger from the context loses the name/kind/method values. Every other method passes `log`.

findings.title: Tests never synchronize with the async legacy write (data race + no coverage)
findings.body: Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection in mode 3 spawn a goroutine that calls the legacy mock. The tests return immediately after the call, so (a) the legacy write is never asserted — mode 3's core behaviour is untested, and (b) the shared `*mock.Mock` is read/written concurrently by the goroutine and by the test's assertions/teardown, which `go test -race` can flag as a data race and causes intermittent panics (mock calls after test completion). Add a synchronization point (e.g. wait channel from the mock's Run/ `assert.Eventually`) and assert the legacy call happened.
